kpis.sub: MP MATERIALS FALLS AS BEIJING MOVES ON ITS CHINESE SHAREHOLDER (SEP 18)
kpis.label: Reuters reported state-owned China Rare Earth Group is in talks to acquire Shenghe Resources — MP's 3% Chinese shareholder — sending MP down 4.3% to $47.26, its lowest since spring and well off the ~$60 August peak. Q2 revenue still doubled YoY to $126.1M with NdPr output +41% and a new gadolinium supply deal signed with a US aerospace/defense manufacturer, so the underlying business is unaffected even as the stock re-rates on the governance overhang. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

Xi Jinping arrives in Washington Sep 24 for his first White House visit in 11 years, departing Sep 25, with rare-earth licensing (yttrium, scandium, neodymium, indium) explicitly on the agenda. Chinese suppliers are still withholding some US-bound shipments as of this week, and expectations for a transformational agreement remain low; the visit lands 47 days before the Nov 10 export-control suspension expiry

Benchmark Mineral Intelligence's battery-grade spot assessment slipped a further 0.8% week-on-week to $19,750/tonne, continuing a decline that has run through most of 2026. Albemarle shares whipsawed on the move — down to $110.91 then up 5.1% to $115.05 in the same week — and Mizuho cut its price target to $140 from $160 on Sep 19

kpis.sub: FREEPORT RECOVERS FROM ITS TARIFF-DOUBT PLUNGE
kpis.label: FCX, Teck, and Southern Copper all fell 7-8% on Sep 10-11 on doubt the White House will finalize a Section 232 refined-copper tariff, but Freeport had recovered to ~$71.50 by Sep 18-19 as copper stabilized and its market cap climbed back above $100B — within 1% of its recent intraday high. Analyst targets now cluster $70-82; the tariff decision itself remains unresolved

themes.title: Xi's Washington visit is now three days out
themes.description: Xi Jinping arrives in Washington Sep 24 and departs Sep 25 — his first White House visit in 11 years, and an unusually compressed one that skips the UN General Assembly entirely. Rare-earth licensing (yttrium, scandium, neodymium, indium) is explicitly on the agenda, but expectations for a transformational agreement are low. The visit lands 47 days before China's expanded export-control suspension expires Nov 10, and 99 days before tougher US defense sourcing rules take effect Jan 1, 2027.

themes.title: China Rare Earth Group moves on MP's Chinese shareholder
themes.description: Reuters reported Sep 18 that state-owned China Rare Earth Group is in talks to acquire Shenghe Resources, which holds a 3% stake in MP Materials, and reportedly wants a controlling position. Shenghe has called the reports "false," but if the deal proceeds it would hand Beijing a passive window into a company where the US Department of Defense is the largest shareholder — and better access to the export quotas Beijing uses to control supply.

themes.title: Chinese shipment halts remain unresolved heading into the summit
themes.description: The Chinese rare-earth suppliers who quietly halted shipments to US buyers in early August — wary of Beijing penalties tied to Responsible Minerals Initiative compliance — have not resumed as of this week. The NdPr magnet complex fell together as a block for the first time since May, a sign pricing momentum is cooling even as the supply picture stays tight. China separately placed MP Materials and USA Rare Earth on an export-control list back in June, a reminder the friction predates and could outlast this month's diplomacy.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + $400M DoD convertible preferred (DoD now largest shareholder, ~15%)
rows.watch for: Fell 4.3% to $47.26 on Sep 18-19 after Reuters reported state-owned China Rare Earth Group is in talks to acquire Shenghe Resources, MP's 3% Chinese shareholder — a new Beijing-consolidation overhang, not an operational one. Q2 revenue doubled YoY to $126.1M, NdPr production +41%, sales volumes +127%, adjusted EBITDA improved $41M, and a new gadolinium oxide supply deal was signed with a US aerospace/defense manufacturer; initial commercial magnet shipments are still guided for Q4. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: The CEO search under interim chief Pol Le Roux (since Jul 1) has now run more than two months with no permanent replacement named, and Amanda Lacaze's transition support formally ends Sep 30 — a hard deadline for the leadership vacuum to resolve or become a real overhang. Record FY26 profit on record average rare-earth-oxide selling prices still hasn't settled the question

Mizuho cut its price target to $140 from $160 on Sep 19 as shares whipsawed — down 3.6-5.6% on the week to $110.91, then up 5.1% to $115.05 as lithium prices steadied. Lithium carbonate itself kept sliding to $19,750/t (-0.8% w/w), continuing a decline that has run through most of 2026. New CEO Ragnar Udd still doesn't take over until Feb 1, 2027; 2026 Atacama guidance of 70,700t LCE remains intact

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: FCX, Teck, and Southern Copper all fell 7-8% Sep 10-11 on doubt the White House will finalize a Section 232 refined-copper tariff, but Freeport recovered to ~$71.50 by Sep 18-19 as copper stabilized, pushing its market cap back above $100B — within 1% of its recent intraday high. Analyst targets now cluster $70-82. The tariff decision itself remains unresolved; the quick recovery is the notable data point this week

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026, priced $17.17)
rows.watch for: Broke ground Sep 9 on a new rare-earth metal/magnet facility in Blacksburg, SC — genuine build-out progress — but filed a fresh SEC registration statement Sep 4 for another securities offering on top of the 126.85M Serra Verde shares, and the stock kept sliding to ~$15.65 (-54% from its $43.98 peak). A Sep 17 mineral-production pact with Pasqal and Riven Systems was also announced. Thras Moraitis becomes CEO Oct 1

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: White Mesa's heavy-rare-earth expansion construction continues, with Phase 1 still slated to enable commercial light and heavy REE output by 2027; pilot output has reached ~29kg of 99.9%-purity Dy oxide, ahead of the 99.5% automotive spec. The Vacuumschmelze (VAC) acquisition remains on track for a Q1 2027 close. No negative catalysts this week — steady execution

Construction keeps hitting concrete milestones: the 198-foot Duplex sulfuric-acid plant stack is anchored, the first crystallizer is installed in the Magnesium Sulfate Building, and one of three high-voltage circuit breakers is in — site remains on track for Q4 2026 energization with 1,600+ workers (2,000+ by year-end). Mechanical completion is still targeted late 2027, and lithium carbonate's continued slide to $19,750/t keeps the cycle-timing question open

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate's global benchmark slipped a further 0.8% to $19,750/t in early September, continuing a decline that has run through most of 2026, and the NdPr magnet complex fell together as a block for the first time since May. Both are reminders that 2026's rare-earth and lithium price strength is not a one-way trade — a producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood the market — or freeze the tap — or just consolidate it
bear_case.description: Chinese suppliers are still withholding some rare-earth shipments from US buyers, while Beijing simultaneously moves to consolidate ownership of Shenghe Resources — MP Materials' 3% Chinese shareholder — through state-owned China Rare Earth Group. Investors betting on any direction here are making a bet on Beijing's posture, not just on markets, and that posture is exactly what's on the table at the Sep 24-25 summit.

bear_case.title: Policy tailwinds aren't guaranteed to arrive
bear_case.description: Freeport's 7-8% plunge on copper-tariff uncertainty (even after its subsequent recovery) shows how much of the sector's bull case rests on policy that hasn't actually been finalized. The same is true elsewhere: MP Materials' 10X plant EBITDA guarantee, Energy Fuels' $725M conditional government support, and Project Vault's $10B EXIM-backed stockpile are all real, but each carries execution and political risk between announcement and cash landing.

bear_case.title: Dilution and leadership overhangs compound
bear_case.description: USA Rare Earth filed a fresh securities registration Sep 4 on top of the 126.85M Serra Verde shares and is down 54% from its peak; Lynas' CEO search under interim chief Pol Le Roux has now run more than two months, with Amanda Lacaze's transition support ending Sep 30; and Albemarle's new CEO doesn't take over until Feb 2027. None of these is disqualifying on its own, but none is resolved either.
